rules.statement: Don't report that a workflow job lacking `environment:` can't reach, or wrongly widens access to, an organization secret when the environment holds no secrets and exists only to scope OIDC federation trust to the job with `id-token: write`.
rules.why: The organization secret is visible to every job in an opted-in repository. In that case the environment only gates the OIDC token, so a job without it, and without `id-token`, gets strictly less access than the gated job, not more.
rules.check: Before reporting, read the workflow's header comment and the job's `permissions` to see where the secret is defined and what the environment is for. Report only if the environment actually holds the secret, or if the job gains `id-token: write` without the environment.

rules.statement: Don't let a workflow job whose run must not be skipped share a concurrency group with a job that uses `cancel-in-progress: true`, or narrow the cancelling job's trigger so it can't fire in the same group.
rules.why: Otherwise a later run in the shared group can silently cancel or replace a running or pending run. Nothing retries it, so its work is lost.
rules.check: Look for jobs with the same `concurrency.group` expression where one sets `cancel-in-progress: true`. Then check whether the cancelling job's `if:` can fire on the same event or state as the job that must complete, for example a comment command on a closed pull request.

rules.statement: Don't leave notes about migrating from older versions in standing code or configuration comments once the code no longer uses those versions; move them to release notes or upgrade documentation.
rules.why: Readers have to work out whether the warning still applies, and the note goes stale.
rules.check: Look for header or inline comments that warn about versions, releases or pins older than the ones the file now uses.

rules.statement: Don't report duplicated conditions between a GitHub Actions job's `if:` and its `concurrency.group` expression when a comment already says the two must stay in sync.
rules.why: Workflow expressions can't share a definition between a job's own `if` and `concurrency`, and a job output can't feed them. Removing the duplication would need a restructure that isn't worth it for a few conditions.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether a nearby comment already says the `if` and `concurrency` expressions must name the same conditions. Report only if the two lists have actually drifted apart, or if no comment links them.
